name: Lateral slit technique

card.summary: A way of cutting hair-transplant recipient sites perpendicular to existing hair so grafts splay out, aiming at denser-looking coverage of a thinning area.
card.note: Surgeons debate slit orientation; it is a surgical procedure performed by clinicians.

quick.overview:
In hair transplantation, the lateral slit technique is a way of making the tiny recipient-site incisions that receive grafts. The slits run across, perpendicular to, existing hairs, and are said to let two to four follicular-unit grafts spread out across the scalp for better coverage.

It became popular in the early 2000s and is the counterpart of the sagittal slit, which runs parallel to existing hairs. The choice is discussed among surgeons, and many reportedly combine both based on the patient.
quick.how: It is done by a surgeon or trained team during a transplant, using micro blades or fine needles to open sites at a planned density, angle and pattern, after which grafts are placed. It is part of a surgical plan, not a home practice.
quick.risks: Wikipedia notes that lateral slits are described as disrupting scalp blood supply more than sagittal slits, and that post-transplant effects can include temporary shock loss. Smoking and alcohol can reduce graft survival, and antibiotics are commonly prescribed afterwards.

lead: The lateral slit technique is a method of creating recipient sites in hair transplant surgery. The surgeon opens very small incisions in the thinning area, then places harvested follicular-unit grafts in them.[1] In lateral slits, the incisions run perpendicular to existing hair, like the crossbar of a T.[1]

People pursue it for hairline and density results: Wikipedia says lateral slits help two to four follicular-unit grafts splay across the scalp, improving coverage.[1] Slit shape, angle and direction also affect whether the new hair looks natural.[1]

The technique became popular in the early 2000s and sits alongside sagittal slits, which run parallel to existing hairs and slide between them, which reduces transection of existing follicles.[1] Wikipedia says the choice is debated and that many experienced surgeons combine both depending on the patient, noting that some of these statements are flagged as unsourced.[1]

chain: Perpendicular incisions in the recipient area
Grafts of 2-4 follicular units placed in them
angle.text: Slit direction is one of the choices a transplant surgeon makes to shape how coverage and density look. It affects how grafts lie and how much existing hair is disturbed.

paras: Recipient sites are made with micro blades or fine needles in a predetermined density and pattern, and technicians usually insert the grafts. Sites are angled consistently so the transplanted hair grows in a natural-looking direction.[1]

Lateral slits are described as perpendicular to existing hair, while sagittal slits are parallel. According to Wikipedia, the advantage claimed for lateral slits is splay and coverage of multi-hair grafts; the drawback claimed is a larger effect on scalp blood supply than sagittal slits.[1]

Transplants are usually harvested by strip (FUT) or follicular unit extraction (FUE). FUT leaves a thin linear donor scar and takes about two weeks to recover, while FUE uses 0.6-1.0 mm punches leaving small dot scars and recovery under a week.[1] Slit technique applies on the recipient side in either case.

Reported effects of transplant surgery include infection risk, for which post-operative antibiotics are commonly prescribed, reduced graft survival with smoking and alcohol, and temporary shock loss of hair.[1]

timeline.event: Lateral slit technique becomes popular in hair transplantation.[1]
